text:
Peyton Krebs has 10 points in 20 games, and 9 of them are assists. That's who he is: a passer with speed (his 44 bursts over 20 mph sit in the 85th percentile), now playing more, about 15 minutes a night over his last ten, up nearly two minutes. He told Audacy's Jeremy and Joe Show about his chemistry with Tage Thompson, and the assists suggest it's real.

The goal column is the odd part. He has 1 goal on 2.93 expected goals (the quality of his chances), shooting 6.7% against a league 13.4%, so his own finishing has been cold. His linemates have been the opposite, scoring more than their chances deserve with him on the ice, which has propped up the assists. Buffalo has had more of the shots with him on at five on five but slightly less than half the chances. Evolving-Hockey had him 93rd among 401 forwards last season, while warning that his results ran ahead of his chances. We'd watch whether the goals catch up before the assists cool off.
